title: BigQuery Internals and Cost: Visual Guide
outline: Title: BigQuery Internals and Cost: Visual Guide

1. Two Planes, One Query | a toggle between one coupled box (the Cloud SQL / AlloyDB / Spanner shape from the storage decision matrix) and BigQuery's separated Colossus storage plane plus Dremel slot pool, with a stepper for concurrent workloads showing who gets starved | storage and compute scale independently and never contend, so every workload gets its own slots over one shared copy of the data instead of sharing a fixed box

2. Pruning The Partitions | 730 daily partitions of a 730 GB events table as a grid, a slider for the filter window, and four filter SHAPES including a function of another column, a subquery join and require_partition_filter | pruning needs a filter the planner can resolve at planning time, and 7 days is ~7 GB instead of 730 GB while a function-wrapped filter silently scans everything at full price

3. Cluster Key Order | 100 blocks of a 1 GB partition clustered by customer_id then event_type, with four WHERE clauses touching the first key, the second key only, both, or neither | cluster keys prune in prefix order like a phone book, and because block pruning happens at run time the dry-run estimate for a clustered table is an upper bound while partition pruning shows up front

4. Baseline Versus Burst | the etl, bi and adhoc reservations from the lesson with a demand slider splitting the bar into baseline, autoscaled, idle and queued slots plus a monthly cost | baseline slots are always billed and buy latency consistency, autoscaled slots bill per second, and a max is what stops one team's runaway queries from touching another's capacity

5. The Break-Even Line | sliders for columns selected and days filtered on a 2 TB 40-column table showing the dry-run arithmetic, over a monthly-scan-volume slider pricing on-demand against 100 baseline slots | on-demand bills bytes at $6.25/TiB so column selection and pruning are the price ($0.10 versus $12.50, a 125x ratio), while capacity bills slot-hours and wins once sustained volume passes the reservation's floor
